clue.text: Nothing divides the lines — that's the idea

indicators.note: nothing divides the lines by sitting between them, so it goes inside the other letters

parts.note: RY, short for railway, is the usual crossword abbreviation for lines
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone reads a blank space between lines of text as the hidden point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lines' is the crossword shorthand for railway lines; 'the idea' looks like the whole definition, but 'the' is used in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a proposed explanation, an idea about how something works.

clue.text: 10 — 7 = 23? Head off in confusion

indicators.note: letters in confusion are jumbled into a new order
taking the head off removes the first letter

parts.note: the answer to 23 across, a word meaning lower

explanation.surface: A sum using clue numbers that seems not to add up, followed by a muddled shrug.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue numbers are arithmetic: 10 minus 7 is the answer. 'Head off' drops the N of NETHER (23 across), leaving ETHER, and 'in confusion' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ten minus seven makes the small number after two, so the sum defines the figure.

clue.text: Without question, a route should be organised as a central line

indicators.note: organising the letters puts them into a new order

explanation.surface: A planner insists a route be laid out down the middle, no question about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without question' reads like 'certainly', but it says the letters come with Q outside the route words; Q joins A ROUTE as fodder for 'should be organised'.
explanation.definitionFit: The equator is the imaginary line running round the middle of the Earth.

clue.text: Press on, having left the last trio of stragglers

parts.note: RE means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: the last trio of a word is its final three letters

explanation.surface: Someone presses on after leaving the final three stragglers behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like a verb with 'on', but it is the noun for journalists. 'the last trio of' takes ERS from stragglers.
explanation.definitionFit: The press is a collective name for journalists and news reporters.

clue.text: Blows kisses

definitions.meaning: blows as in punches or slaps
noisy kisses, as in a smacker on the cheek

explanation.surface: Someone blowing kisses at a departing friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Smacks are hard slaps, and also loud kisses in informal speech.

clue.text: Bottoms up, endlessly — that's the watchword!

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom
endlessly drops the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A drinking toast offered as a slogan to live by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' leaves OTTOM from Bottoms, and 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A motto is a short saying adopted as a guiding principle, a watchword.

clue.text: London landlord that's facing sentence?

parts.note: London is the capital city of the UK
a landlord is one who lets property out

explanation.surface: A London landlord in the dock, waiting to hear the judge's sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facing sentence' suggests a criminal awaiting punishment; it means standing at the front of a written sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: An upper-case initial stands at the start of every written sentence.

clue.text: Steps we took (cancelling agreement) in order to find best contact place

indicators.note: putting letters in order means arranging them afresh
cancelling a word removes it from the letters

parts.note: OK is a word of agreement

explanation.surface: Someone retraces their steps after a deal falls through, hunting for the ideal place to meet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cancelling agreement' takes OK out of TOOK, and 'in order' rearranges STEPS WE TO.
explanation.definitionFit: On a bat or racket, the spot giving the cleanest strike on the ball is called this.

clue.text: Party embracing a limit on spending from the beginning

indicators.note: embracing means holding the other letters within

parts.note: a do is a party
a cap is a ceiling placed on spending

explanation.surface: A party held on a budget that limits what can be spent.
explanation.definitionFit: In music this Italian instruction tells players to go back and repeat from the start.

clue.text: Run at it wildly, picking up speed and winning

indicators.note: picking up takes the other letters on board, inside
running wildly means the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: mph, miles per hour, measures speed

explanation.surface: A runner charges at something, gathering pace, and comes out on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' makes TRIUANT from RUN AT IT, and 'picking up' takes MPH into the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone triumphant has won and is celebrating the victory.

clue.text: Member of the Lords backtracking on record

indicators.note: backtracking means going back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: RE means on or about
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A member of the House of Lords goes back on what they said for the record.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer sits in the House of Lords by virtue of a title such as baron or earl.

clue.text: See 6
He no longer believes in a position Sartre oddly rejected

parts.note: a post is a job or position

indicators.note: rejecting the odd letters keeps only the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: A man rejects his faith after reading Sartre, though only in fits and starts.
explanation.walkthrough: Sartre was an atheist philosopher, which strengthens the surface. 'oddly rejected' keeps ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostate is someone who has abandoned their religious faith or former beliefs.

clue.text: Show disapproval, and put money where mouth is?

definitions.meaning: to tighten the mouth in displeasure
taken literally, a money bag held against the mouth

explanation.surface: Someone frowns at a scheme and then backs their opinion with cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'put your money where your mouth is' means back your words; here it is read literally, a wallet at the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Pursing the lips, puckering them tight, is a familiar sign of disapproval.

clue.text: No being cryptic and causing problems!

parts.note: the clue word is the result: the word on (playing, as an actor is on stage) written up in a down light becomes this

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to talk plainly and makes trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being cryptic' tells you to read the answer as instructions: ON, meaning playing, set upwards gives the clue's No.
explanation.definitionFit: Children or machines playing up are misbehaving and giving trouble.

clue.text: See 13
For this reason lack of amplification is conducive to working

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore
a lack of something means no such thing
a mic, a microphone, amplifies a voice

explanation.surface: A quiet office without loudspeakers is said to help people get work done.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergonomic design suits the human body so that people can work comfortably and efficiently.

clue.text: Cheese cut & grated

indicators.note: grated cheese is shredded, so the letters are broken up and rearranged
cut removes the last letter of the word

parts.note: the symbol is called an ampersand

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction: cheese, cut and grated.
explanation.walkthrough: The '&' must be spelt out: 'cut' loses its last letter, D, leaving AMPERSAN, and 'grated' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Parmesan is a hard Italian cheese usually served grated.

clue.text: Omit state (not Rhode Island) at beginning of trip

indicators.note: not means the following letters are left out

parts.note: Missouri is a US state
RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Planning a US road trip that skips Rhode Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not Rhode Island' takes RI out of MISSOURI.
explanation.definitionFit: To miss something out is to leave it out or skip it.

clue.text: Doctor, can I get the first pair to inject essential nutrient?

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered
the first pair of a word is its opening two letters

explanation.surface: A patient asks the doctor for an injection of a vital vitamin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the person addressed but is the anagram signal: CAN I becomes NIAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Niacin, vitamin B3, is a nutrient the body needs from food.

clue.text: One's offered hospitality in rogue state

indicators.note: the letters are found in the words that follow

explanation.surface: A visitor is welcomed in a pariah nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest is someone who is welcomed and looked after in another's home.

clue.text: Dropped dead while antidote was working? Bother!

indicators.note: working letters are being worked over into a new arrangement
dropped means taken out of the word

explanation.surface: Someone collapsed and died just as the antidote began to take effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropped dead' reads as dying, but it removes D from ANTIDOTE before 'was working' rearranges ANTIOTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that eats into you nags and troubles you, as in asking what is eating you.

clue.text: Those living abroad get help returning, with first instalments of support payments of regular amounts

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: aid is help

indicators.note: the first instalment of each word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Emigrants receive help in the form of regular support payments.
explanation.definitionFit: A diaspora is a people scattered away from their homeland.

clue.text: The main problem with canoe

indicators.note: a problem with the canoe is something wrong with it, so its letters are disordered

explanation.surface: The chief difficulty is with the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main problem' reads as 'the chief difficulty', but 'The main' is the definition: the main is an old word for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: In poetic usage the main means the open sea, so the high seas.

clue.text: Lower numbers

parts.note: N is the usual abbreviation for number
the anaesthetic gas is a number in the sense of a thing that numbs

explanation.surface: An instruction to bring numbers down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'numbers' is read twice: N (number) and ETHER, a 'number' because it makes you numb, a crossword classic.
explanation.definitionFit: Nether is an old word for lower or under, as in the nether regions.

clue.text: Opposing odds when odds are extremely short

definitions.meaning: the even numbers, as against the odd ones
a betting price of one to one, very short odds

explanation.surface: A bettor weighs taking on the bookmaker when the price is very short.
explanation.definitionFit: Even numbers are the opposite of odd ones, and a bet at even money pays back its stake.

clue.text: Finally, "Hi ho Silver" before the charge!

indicators.note: before puts the first piece in front of the other

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of each word

explanation.surface: The Lone Ranger cries 'Hi ho Silver' as he urges his horse into the charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hi ho Silver' is the Lone Ranger's cry to his horse.
explanation.definitionFit: An agio is a fee or premium charged for exchanging one currency for another.

clue.text: Did men live sinfully, being intent on wrongdoing?

indicators.note: acting sinfully is going astray, so the letters stray into another order

explanation.surface: A question about whether men lived sinfully with wicked purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with malicious thoughts and intentions is described as having a wicked mind.

clue.text: Set theory was deceptive

parts.note: to set something down is to put it
the answer to the clue at 1 ... in this grid

explanation.surface: Set theory in mathematics turned out to be misleading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theory' points to the grid: it is the answer at 1 across, so it gives the words ONE ACROSS.
explanation.definitionFit: To put one across someone is to trick or deceive them.

clue.text: See 27
